# GitHub Copilot Instructions for Vista API

## Project Overview

It's a RESTful API-first project built with [Hono](https://hono.dev) deployed on serverless edge servers from Cloudflare Workers, that implements the [OpenAPI specification](https://swagger.io/specification/) defined in the [vista-spec](https://github.com/joelmanasdbarrio/vista-spec) project generating [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) interfaces for DTOs, and response objects, as well asquery, path and body parameters, based on the specification's schema.

### Purpose and Goals

- Serve as the backend API for the Vista's web and mobile applications
- Provide secure and efficient API endpoints for data access and manipulation on Supabase PostgreSQL database
- Implement real-time updates for map and notifications changes
- Act as an intermediary service for authentication and authorization through Supabase Auth

## Folder Structure

- `src/` - Contains the main source code for the API
  - `db/schema.ts` - Database schema and migrations using Drizzle ORM
  - `modules/` - Domain-driven designed modules for different API functionalities.
    \
    Each module may contain:
    - `*.router.ts` - Exports a Router class exposing the module's Hono router, in charge of handling the HTTP requests and responses, as well as input data validation using the `validate` helper from `src/utils/error_handling/middlewares/validator.middleware.ts`
    - `*.controller.ts` - Exports a Controller class that implements `BaseController` abstract class from `src\modules\base.controller.ts` , which acts as an intermediary between the router and the service layer, handling request processing and response formatting
    - `*.service.ts` - Exports a Service class that implements `BaseService` abstract class `src\modules\base.service.ts`, which contains the business logic and interacts with the repository layer for data access and manipulation and other services if needed
    - `*.repository.ts` - Exports a Repository class that implements `BaseRepository` abstract class from `src\modules\base.repository.ts`, which interacts with the database using Drizzle ORM and mapper layer to switch between database entities and DTOs
    - `*.mapper.ts` - Exports a Mapper class that implements `BaseMapper` abstract class from `src\modules\base.mapper.ts`, which maps database entities to DTOs and vice versa. The application will always work with DTOs instead of database entities
    - `lib/*.validations.ts` - Contains validation schemas for request data using Zod, which are used in the router and controller layers to validate incoming requests
    - Another submodule, which may contain the same structure as above, but focused on a specific, related functionality of the module
    \
    Available modules:
    - `account/` - Personal and Enterprise accounts management
    - `auth/` - Authentication and authorization middlewares with Supabase Auth
    - `activities/` - Activity management
      - `activityCategories/` - Activity categories management
      - `activityParticipants/` - Activity participants management
    - `establishments/` - Establishment management
      - `establishmentRequests/` - Establishment requests management
      - `addresses/` - Address management for establishments
    - `follows/` - User follow management
      - `followRequests/` - Follow requests management
    - `notifications/` - Notification management
  - `types/` - TypeScript interfaces and types
    - `schema/vista-spec.schema.ts` - Autogenerated Typecript schema based on `@joelmanasdbarrio/vista-spec/openapi/openapi-rest.yaml` using openapi-typescript (`npm run types:generate`)
    - `vista-spec.types.ts` - Exports ready-to-use interfaces from the `schema/vista-spec.schema.ts`
    - `hono.types.ts` - Declares context variable types
    - `database.types.ts` - Exports Typescript interfaces for database tables inferred from Drizzle's database schema `src/db/schema.ts`
  - `utils/` - Utility functions and helpers
    - `error_handling/` - Error handling utilities
      - `middlewares/` - Middlewares for error handling
      - `AppError.ts` - Custom error class for the application
    - `logger.ts` - Logger utility for logging messages and errors
  - `index.ts` - Main entry point for the API
- `drizzle/` - Drizzle ORM autogenerated and custom migrations
- `drizzle.config.ts` - Drizzle ORM configuration file
- `.dev.vars` - Local Wrangler environment variables for development
- `.env` - Local environment variables for Drizzle database connection
- `.eslintrc.cjs` - ESLint configuration file
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration file
- `wrangler.jsonc` - Wrangler configuration file for Cloudflare Workers deployment

## Modules

### Accounts

User accounts are responsible for creating and managing Activities and Establishments in the Vista social network.

Users can search for accounts using their name and username in the search bar.
Each user account has its own profile page, where they can see their personal information, such as name, username, and biography, as well as their list of followers/followings, published Activities and managed Establishments (if applies) as long as they have their visibility set to public.
They can also update and delete their own account and managed entities at any time.

Information collected from users:
- Name.
- Username.
- Email address.
- Birth date.
- Biography.
- Profile picture.
- Website.
- Password.
- Visibility settings (public or private).

As well as user additional preferences such as language, notifications, and theme settings.

There can be two types of accounts in the Vista social network: Personal and Enterprise.

#### Personal Accounts

This account **represents a physical person**, being the only account that **can interact with other entities**, such as joining activities and following other users.

It also has the ability to create its own Activities, as long as they don't take place at a specific Establishment.
That is, if a user with a Personal account wants to create an Activity in a physical location, they must locate it at a generic coordinate on the map.

This is because there is no way of checking when a Personal account has rights over a private property to act on its behalf and publish an Activity in that location.

##### Follows

All Personal accounts have the ability to follow other accounts, which allows them to see their published Activities in their feed and receive notifications when they publish new ones.

When an account is set to private, only its followers will be able to see its lists of followers/followings, published Activities, Activity entries, and managed Establishments (if applies).
If a user wants to follow a private account, they must send a follow request first, to be accepted or rejected by the account owner.

#### Enterprise Accounts

This account **represents legal entities**, such as businesses, brands, associations or organizations, and public figures. It also has the ability to **create and manage Establishments**, and organize Activities in them.

To create an Activity or an Establishment, the Enterprise account must be verified by Vista's trusted partner: _to be discussed (Onfido, Trulioo or Veriff)_.

### Activities

They are the main entities of the Vista social network. They can be created by Personal and Enterprise accounts and take place at an online website, in a generic location or in an Establishment.

Information collected from Activities:
- Owner account.
- Name.
- Description.
- Category.
- Language.
- Images.
- Location (online, generic coordinate or Establishment).
- Date and time (start/end)
- Price:
  - Currency.
  - Amount (min/max).
- Participants (min/max).
- Age restriction (if applicable).

All Activities will be displayed in a list format, with the ones with the most entries being shown first.
Physical Activities will also be shown on an interactive map, side by side with the list, identified by a pin icon of its Category.

Users can search for Activities filtering by their name, description, category, language, location, date start/end, price min/max, entries (min/max), following accounts only, and in case of physical Activities they can also use the map.
Only Activities published by private accounts will not be visible to users unless they are currently following that account.
Each Activity has its own profile page, where users can see information about it in greater detail and join it.

#### Categories

All Activities are classified (among other things) into categories, which are used to group them by their type.
Categories are also organized as a tree structure, where each category can have one additional layer of subcategories.
Subcategories are the ones that will be used to classify the Activities and will be shown in the list of Activities and in the map.
Each parent category is named after a generic kind of activity and has a color associated with it, which is used to easily identify it.
Meanwhile, subcategories are named after a more specific kind of activity and will use the same color as their parent category as well as a representative icon.

## Establishments

An Establishment is a physical location (building or private property) where an Activity can take place. They are created and managed by Enterprise accounts and thus may or may not be visible depending on the visibility settings of the owner's account.

Users can also search for Establishments using their name or direction in the search bar. Each Establishment has its own profile page, where users can see the Activities that take place in it.

Information collected from Establishments:
- Owner account.
- Name.
- Address:
  - Country.
  - Zip code.
  - City.
  - Street (name and number).
  - Block (if applicable).
  - Stair (if applicable).
  - Floor (if applicable).
  - Door (if applicable).
  - Coordinates (latitude and longitude).

The combination of all the address fields (except for coordinates) are used to make up for a unique identifier of the Establishment.

## Tools, Libraries, and Frameworks

- [Hono](https://hono.dev) - Lightweight web framework for building APIs
- [Drizzle ORM](https://orm.drizzle.team) - TypeScript ORM for PostgreSQL database interactions on Supabase database
- [Zod](https://zod.dev) - TypeScript-first schema declaration and validation
- [Supabase JS](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/start) - User management and authentication with email & password / OAuth providers (Google, X, Facebook, etc.)
- [OpenAPI Specification](https://swagger.io/specification/) - API definition standard
- [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) - Superset of JavaScript for type safety and modern features
- [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) - Linting tool for maintaining code quality
- [Wrangler](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/) - CLI tool for managing Cloudflare Workers projects
- [ts-standard](https://github.com/standard/ts-standard) - TypeScript style guide, linter, and formatter based on [StandardJS](https://standardjs.com/)

### Development and Deployment

Install dependencies and run the development server:

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Generate and execute Drizzle migrations based on the schema:

```bash
npm run drizzle:generate
npm run drizzle:migrate
```

Generate TypeScript types from OpenAPI specification:

```bash
npm run types:generate
```

This command will execute `openapi-typescript` to create the `./src/types/schema/vista-spec.schema.ts` file with all the interfaces and types needed to work with the API.
Once you execute the command, note that `openapi-typescript` package has an error by default where the discriminator is duplicated in the generated schema with 2 different values, which may cause errors in the source code. In that case, you will need to manually rename the duplicated discriminator from the generated file to just 'type'. As a general rule, always rename the property with the shortest value, for example:

```diff
- accountType: 'personal'
- accountType: 'AccountPersonalDTO'
+ type: 'personal'
+ accountType: 'AccountPersonalDTO'
```

## Development Guidelines

Take `src/modules/accounts` module as reference

### TypeScript Standards

- Use **strict TypeScript** with proper type definitions
- Prefer **explicit typing** over `any`, always use interfaces provided in `src/types/**` or `*.validations.ts` files
- Use **interfaces** for complex object structures
- Follow **camelCase** for variables and functions
- Use **PascalCase** for classes and interfaces
- Extend from **abstract classes** in `src/modules/base.*` when possible
- Follow **eslint and ts-standard** rules defined in `.eslintrc.cjs` for formatting and code style

### Code Organization

- **Modules**: Follow Domain-Driven Design (DDD) principles, each module should encapsulate its own functionality
  - Each module should have its own directory under `src/modules/` or be a submodule of an existing one
- **Routers**: Use `*.router.ts` files to define Hono routers for handling HTTP requests and responses
- **Controllers**: Use `*.controller.ts` files to implement the `BaseController` abstract class from `src/modules/base.controller.ts`, which acts as an intermediary between the Router and the Service layer, handling request processing and response formatting
- **Services**: Use `*.service.ts` files to implement the `BaseService` abstract class from `src/modules/base.service.ts`, which contains the business logic and interacts with the repository layer for data access and manipulation and other services if needed
- **Repositories**: Use `*.repository.ts` files to implement the `BaseRepository` abstract class from `src/modules/base.repository.ts`, which interacts with the database using Drizzle ORM and mapper layer to switch between database entities and DTOs
- **Mappers**: Use `*.mapper.ts` files to implement the `BaseMapper` abstract class from `src/modules/base.mapper.ts`, which maps database entities to DTOs and vice versa. The application will always work with DTOs instead of database entities
- **Validations**:
  - Use `*.validations.ts` files to define Zod schemas for each CRUD request validation and type safety, which are used in the Router (request parameters and Hono context), Controller (Hono context and function return types), and Service (request parameters) layers to validate incoming requests
  - **Types**: Use `*.types.ts` files to define TypeScript interfaces and types for the module, which are used in the Service (response DTOs and enums), Repository (request parameters, DTOs and enums), and Mapper (DTOs, enums and database table interfaces) layers to ensure type safety
- **Error Handling**: Always use `src/utils/error_handling/AppError.ts` for throwing errors, and handle them in the global middleware `src/utils/error_handling/middlewares/errorHandler.middleware.ts`
- **Async/Await**: Prefer over Promises for better readability
- **Logging**: Always use `src/utils/logger.ts` for logging messages and errors

### Naming Conventions

- Files: KebabCase for files (`module.layer.ts`)
- Variables/Functions: camelCase (`createNotification`, `notificationId`)
- Classes: PascalCase (`NotificationController`)
- Constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for enums and constants (`FOLLOW_REQUEST`)
- Endpoints: kebabCase in URLs (`/follow-requests`)
- Use `readonly` modifier for private unmodifiable variables in classes

### User Authentication Workflow

1. User authenticates against Supabase Auth using its login preferred method (email/password or OAuth service)
2. If login was successful, Supabase Auth responds with a JWT token
3. Vista frontend applications (web and mobile apps) send this JWT with every request
4. Vista API validates the authenticity and validity of the token on protected routes with `protectedRoute` middleware from `src/modules/auth/auth.middleware.ts`
5. If the token is valid, the request is processed, otherwise an error is returned

### Required Dependencies

- **Hono**: Always use Cloudflare Workers edge-serverless compliant code, following the Hono framework conventions, avoiding unavailable Node.js APIs and features.
